sessions.title: Improvers 1
sessions.details:
Improvers 1 is for adults who are confident and polished with all the Beginners material up to and including Pre-Improvers and are ready to build on pirouettes, work on more challenging adage in the centre and start batterie. Some will benefit from attending Pre-Improvers alongside or instead, if not quite strong or polished enough yet.  There are supporting handouts and videos for each lesson. 

 You should already have attended the Complete Beginners Pointe course after Pre-Improvers on Mondays and/or be confident with relevé in retiré sideways at the barre and echappé sin the centre, before booking the Beginners Pointe class that follows. sessions.title: Improvers 2
sessions.details: This class is for adults who have successfully mastered all the elements in Improvers 1 and are competent with double pirouettes and ready to learn fouettés, more complex batterie such as brisé and entrechat trois and more challenging grand allegro such as grand jeté en tournant, grand fouetté sauté and saut de basque. You should attend at least twice a week to be strong enough for this level; can also be taken with Improvers 1 if less advanced or with Advanced 1 if more experienced. Those attending pointework afterwards must already be sufficiently skilled and strong enough for relevés on one leg in the centre. This course is also suitable for ballet-fit returning dancers who received vocational training to a high level. A special discount package is available on Tuesdays which starts at 6.30pm with Ballet Floor-barre, followed by Improvers 2 Class & Elementary Pointe which comes with a saving of £35. (Repertoire will return in the Autumn term) • Place: Capital City College (Holloway), 444 Camden Road, London, N7 0SP • Dates: 15th September - 1st December 2026(11 lessons; no class 27 Oct) • Cost: £185 / £250 • Teacher: Serena Cundari

sessions.title: 5Rhythms with Flow
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • In 5Rhythms, we hand over prayer to the body, allowing it to become our wisest teacher. Through movement, we invite the body to express its unique rhythm in the present moment, uncovering its often suppressed intelligence.Flow Vulk brings her own energy and vision to the dance. In her words:"I found my feet on a 5Rhythms dance floor in 2014. This is when and where it all magnificently fell apart before falling into place and making sense. It is in our bones, blood and breath - the beat, the rhythm, the Song of Songs. The Song of Life. Dance it. This is how we wake up, how we become alive again, how we find answers and resolutions. We dance not to forget but to remember, not to get lost but to find ourselves, not to disappear but to arise in our full, authentic glory. So let this be an open invitation to shake off the cobwebs, rattle those bones, let that breath flow and let your feet find their beat. Let Life In."All are welcome, whether you’re new to 5Rhythms or have danced it for years.In 5Rhythms, we hand over prayer to the body, allowing it to become our wisest teacher. sessions.title: Jin Mai Gong Qigong (8-Week Course)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • JIN MAI GONG QIGONGAn Eight-Week Qigong Course with Natalia Miralles Huete📅 Course dates: 8 sessions from 3 September to 29 October (no class on 1 October)🕑 Time: 18:30 - 19:30📍 Location: Top Studio, Colet HouseJoin Natalia at Colet House from 3 September to learn a traditional yet little-known Qigong system called Jin Mai Gong that will help restore the free flow of energy throughout your body.Qigong is an ancient Chinese art for energy cultivation. This vital energy, known as Qi (or Chi), flows continuously throughout the body via a network of channels that act like a vast system of rivers and tributaries, nourishing our whole organism.Some of these channels are called meridians and are responsible for supplying our internal organs with Qi in a smooth and continuous way. When this flow of Qi becomes excessive, deficient or blocked, the body's balance is disrupted and illness may arise.In this eight-week course, you will learn six essential Qigong exercises that help keep the energy of the main organs of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) flowing smoothly through their meridians, preventing blockages and, consequently, the development of illness.We will work specifically on the six tendino-muscular (sinew) meridians associated with the six Yin organs: the Lungs, Spleen, Heart, Kidneys, Xin Bao (Heart Protector) and Liver.These tendino-muscular meridians are made up of the tendons, muscles and fascia that surround the main meridians. Using effective stretches together with circular and spiralling movements, we will help release restrictions in these tissues, allowing Qi to flow more freely through the meridians.Benefits of this system:Releases blockages and restores the free flow of Qi through the meridians, improving the function of the internal organs.Improves the emotional states associated with energetic imbalances in the internal organs.Helps eliminate excess fat and toxins accumulated in the fascia.Strengthens the immune system by supporting the body's defensive energy (Wei Qi) in the subcutaneous layers.Supports recovery from muscular tension, ligament problems, inflammation and joint weakness.Promotes greater freedom of movement throughout the body.JIN MAI GONG QIGONGAn Eight-Week Qigong Course with Natalia Miralles Huete📅 Course dates: 8 sessions from 3 September to 29 October (no class on 1 October)🕑 Time: 18:30 - 19:30📍 Location: Top Studio, Colet HouseJoin Natalia at Colet House from 3 September to learn a traditional yet little-known Qigong system called Jin Mai Gong that will help restore the free flow of energy throughout your body.Qigong is an ancient Chinese art for energy cultivation. sessions.title: Culture Remix: Voice & Song Circle
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • CULTURE REMIX: VOICE & SONG CIRCLEA fortnightly collective of voice and unityA space to come back to yourself and rise together through resonance in choral harmony. Through song and voice, this circle offers a simple way to release, connect, and land - no performance, no right way to do it, just presence and shared vibes.Alongside singing, breathwork and light exercises support expression and presence - helping everyone in the room find their own voice, harmonies, frequencies and depth of connection to self and the group. There will be a cultural mix of repertoires and styles to explore.The circle includes:✦ Song and voice - open to all, no experience needed✦ Presence and expression - light exercises to help you arrive and open up✦ Conversation and wordplay - space to be heard and to listen✦ Science and Soul - looking at frequencies, breath and depth of sound✦ Rhythm and Roots - using key principles of heartbeat and groundingWhy it matters: In a fast-moving, over-productive world, this is a space to put all of that down - to reconnect with your own voice and a sense of freedom, all in a way that asks nothing of you but your presence.Come as you are.Format: Fortnightly | Thursday eveningsVenue: Colet HouseJimi LyonsA graduate of the British Academy of New Music and recipient of its National Music Facilitator of the Year award, Jimi Lyons has spent over five decades as a respected musician and mentor at the heart of the UK music industry, co-founding the iconic Vibes & Pressure at Passing Clouds, Dalston with Natty. He's led drum and song circles worldwide in both Nyabinghi and other cultural, spiritual and musical traditions and worked alongside industry cornerstones such as Sade, Julian Marley, Danny Sims, Dennis Brown and Bunny Wailer, to name a few. Jimi brings that depth of experience into the circle with warmth and ease — holding space for voice and play, and opening the room to connection and presence.Trinity GoldieTransformation strategist for individuals and organisations, and conscious music facilitator and artist, Trinity Goldie has spent over three decades building community through sound, somatics and self-healing practice. Her foundations are rooted in kirtan and bhajans from her early quests, aged 19, to India and Tibet, however is always exploring new ways to connect to our heart and purpose. Trinity specialises in curating experiences, workshops and retreats that support individuals and groups in coming back to a space of wholesome resonance and remembering.CULTURE REMIX: VOICE & SONG CIRCLEA fortnightly collective of voice and unityA space to come back to yourself and rise together through resonance in choral harmony. sessions.title: The Yoga of Vocal Sound, Music and Meditation
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • Are you ready to embark on a journey of self-transformation? Join James D’Angelo – a leading authority on sound healing – in uncovering one of the great aspects of attaining true sound health through the tuning of the chakras.In this unique workshop, James will introduce you to vocal homeopathy, and its processes by which the chakras are stimulated and re-tuned, clearing blockages and releasing fine energies. Alongside the therapeutic use of voice, he will bring in embodiment practices with Chi Kung-like movements integrating them into the toning practices. Finally, and complementary to the chakra work, you will experience samples of Taoist healing sounds/movements. Learning mantras for the subtle energy field, and drawing vocal sound within as a form of meditation.No previous experience is necessary, only a deep intent to be your true Self.James D’Angelo has been leading his Soundspirit courses in the UK, Europe and the USA since 1996 and is considered a leading authority on sound healing practices. sessions.title: Drum Circle (6-session series)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • Get ready to drum up some rhythm at our Drum Circle event! Immerse yourself in a beat-packed 6-session series – whether you're in for the whole groove with full-course tickets or feel like jamming spontaneously with our drop-in tickets. Let's keep the vibe rhythmic!Alternate Thursdays 19:30 - 21:00, West Studio (Sept 24th - Dec 3rd)Our African Drum Circle workshop in London gives you the chance to learn to play the African “Djembe” Drum. Explore the “bass, tone, slap” sounds of this instrument and discover why African drumming is irresistible.Drumming is a great way to release stress and develop creativity, and it’s also the oldest form of communal musical bonding. The class will also include time to dance, shake and move to the beat.Drums are provided. No experience needed!With Ailon & KayKay SmithI have been playing djembe for 15 years and love to perform and teach. I like to describe my drum circle sessions as an introduction to the Joys of Djembe. I love what I do and it makes me happy to be able to share my passion with others. My goal is to create an enjoyable experience for all levels and experience of participants.Ailon FreeFor the last 30 years, Ailon’s professional life has been devoted to the synthesis of spiritual practice with creative self expression. sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • A Calling Home – The Body as Home is a Somatic Activated Healing™ (SAH Method) practice, a trauma-informed, body-based approach that blends: somatic movement breath work mantra and meditation music and free, intuitive movement.Rather than intellectualizing or talking about emotions, this practice invites the body to lead, allowing sensations and stored emotions to be expressed and gently released through movement. We work from a bottom-up approach, using the body and felt sensations as the entry point, rather than analyzing thoughts or revisiting specific traumatic memories. As a certified SAH Method™ teacher, I guide participants to “drop the story and be with the feeling,” creating a safe space for emotions to move without re-engaging with the narratives around them. Participants can expect a guided, supportive experience that helps to: ground and regulate the nervous system reconnect with physical sensations gently release what has been held in the body cultivate moments of safety, steadiness, and embodied presence There is no choreography, no performance, and no “right way” to move. This session is an invitation to move, shake, soften, and play, to let energy flow more freely through the body, release what feels stuck, and reconnect with joy, aliveness, and a sense of home within.Still wondering what to expect? sessions.title: Playfulness for Beginners (4-week course)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • 7.15-9.00pm on Wednesdays June 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24thWho says your spiritual practice needs to be serious? What if playfulness could become a pathway towards self-discovery and wholeness?Come and join us for this 4-week introductory ‘practice of playfulness' journey, where grown up adults can reconnect with their often buried sense of childlike play. We will draw from the worlds of clowning, improv, mime and dance as well as spontaneous silliness and generalised irreverence. Together, this unlikely cocktail will leave you feeling joyous, open-hearted and flooded with endorphins.Through a range of games and structures, we will explore aspects of play such as spontaneity, misbehaviour, exuberance, sensitivity, connection and totality - and also take time to explore and process how we are feeling as we undergo the journey.The workshops will be a safe space with no pressure ‘to perform’- although the urge may arise. Rather the aim is to build an encouraging supportive nest from which you can launch yourself into your innately exuberant and playful aspect and free your inner child.Some aspects of the workshop will be held and structured, others will be a little bit free and spontaneous (and even occasionally anarchic), all interspersed with dancing and 'digestion time.' There will also be a chill-out area should you need to sit things out for a while ************* During this course you will: Discover how The Practice of Playfulness is a healing medicine that can transform emotions such as repression, numbness and disconnection into feelings of happiness, optimism and inner aliveness.See how the path of self-expression develops inner qualities such as courage, creativity, confidence and improved communication skills.Understand how play gives a strong taste of emotional freedom and moment-by-moment living in a real, embodied way.Be supported through regular sharing circles and times for self-reflection. ************* Read other people's experience of the course:“I believe that what Ailon is offering is incredibly powerful and if you want to live life with a bit more lightheartedness then you should definitely go along to his workshops!”“Thank you for an enriching and ridiculous 6 weeks of playfulness.I loved the journey and cultivating the trust to play together allowed fresh and unexpected expressions to emerge.”“For me this is less of a class or workshop and more of a happening…a congregation of joyful souls happy to hang out and relax in a climate of friendliness. Out of that trust, true silliness and fun can emerge.”“Thank you for bringing into fruition a space which is so playful and nourishing to the soul. To have all our parts to come up and be met, not only with with encouragement but with love is so rare in this world- it takes weird and deep to awaken and meet weird and deep!”“ It’s been a pleasure being on this journey with every single one of you and see everyone expand and grow on this journey into deeper expression of our selves. I appreciate everyone’s acceptance and kindness. It’s been the first place in a long time where I felt safe and accepted to just be myself and explore parts of myself no matter how crazy, silly and unexpected.”"Ailon creates such a safe and humorous space for people to explore their inner joker and let go of their inhibitions. sessions.title: Baduanjin Qigong (8-week course)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • BADUANJIN QIGONG – The Eight Silk BrocadesAn Eight-Week Qigong Course with Natalia Miralles Huete📅 Course dates: 8 classes from 9 April to 11 June (No class on 23 April and 4 June)18:30 – 19:30📍 Location: Top Studio, Colet HouseBaduanjin, also known as “The Eight Silk Brocades”, is an ancient Qigong set of eight different fluid movements that together condition the whole body externally — stretching and strengthening it — and internally, improving the function of the organs and systems (respiratory, circulatory, digestive, nervous, etc.).The set was first described in an eighth-century Taoist text, and it is known to have been used effectively throughout the 17th century during wars in China to alleviate soldiers’ fatigue. This is a key aspect of Qigong, as it helps us to regain energy and vitality to go about our modern daily lives and face our inner battles of stress and emotional challenges.Baduanjin represents an excellent short daily health routine. It will provide you with a whole-body workout, mobilising all your joints, strengthening your muscles and bones, and improving your posture and balance, while helping to focus and calm your busy mind. Your emotions will also feel more balanced, and your energy levels will increase.Once you have learnt the set, it will take you just 20 minutes to complete, although the practice can be shorter or longer depending on the number of repetitions. If you persevere in practising the set daily or a few times per week after the course, you will soon notice the health benefits it brings.The course also includes the essential foundations for effective Qigong practice: breathing techniques, preparatory self-massage, structured joint-opening exercises, and the “three regulations” — body, breath and mind — providing a clear and methodical framework for practising Baduanjin safely and efficiently.BADUANJIN QIGONG – The Eight Silk BrocadesAn Eight-Week Qigong Course with Natalia Miralles Huete📅 Course dates: 8 classes from 9 April to 11 June (No class on 23 April and 4 June)18:30 – 19:30📍 Location: Top Studio, Colet HouseBaduanjin, also known as “The Eight Silk Brocades”, is an ancient Qigong set of eight different fluid movements that together condition the whole body externally — stretching and strengthening it — and internally, improving the function of the organs and systems (respiratory, circulatory, digestive, nervous, etc.).The set was first described in an eighth-century Taoist text, and it is known to have been used effectively throughout the 17th century during wars in China to alleviate soldiers’ fatigue. sessions.title: The Movements
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • Meditation through movementThe Movements are a collection of sacred dances, exercises, prayers and their accompanying music that originated from various schools, dervish orders and monasteries across the Middle East and Central Asia. They were collected and brought to the West by the philosopher and mystic, G.I. Gurdjieff. They were first taught in England to Ouspensky’s pupils at Lyne Place and Colet House in the 1930s. The Study Society is unique in teaching the early repertoire of Movements as they were originally taught, in an unchanged line to the present day.The Movements provide a non-verbal way of experiencing the essence of the Fourth Way teaching. They convey knowledge about the great universal laws and can be a vehicle for expressing universal truths. They can be thought of as a special form of ‘moving meditation’. Through the practice of attention they can enable participants to experience the working of finer energies, bringing all parts of the human organism into a more harmonious whole.The Study Society offers these evenings free of charge, but you are invited to make a donation to support the charity in its works.Meditation through movementThe Movements are a collection of sacred dances, exercises, prayers and their accompanying music that originated from various schools, dervish orders and monasteries across the Middle East and Central Asia. Suitable if: You are 18+ and you’ve never taken a contemporary class before, or you’ve been once or twice and want to go back to basics. Jonathan is a professional dancer with over 5 years of international performance experience in Theatre, Outdoor Production, TV & Film and Gallery Performance. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. Changing facilities are available on the first floor. A water fountain is available on the second floor- please bring your own reuse-able bottle for this. You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. Please make sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Please note, as the studios are used by our professional dancers we ask that you refrain from using hair products and body lotions as these can make the floor slippery. Terms and Conditions of Booking If you need to cancel your booking, you can do so up to 48 hours before a drop in and up to 48 hours before the first class of a term booking for a full refund in class credits by logging into your Momence account. If you'd prefer a monetary refund, just email us to let us know.

sessions.title: Ballet Improvers
sessions.details: Nina’s upbeat class will explore placement, spatial expansion, lyricism, and musicality. The focus will be on artistic expression, and how correct technique and coordination facilitates pace and speed. Nina began as an actress and dancer, appearing in over 60 TV, film, and stage productions before moving on to teach and coach ballet companies and dancers. Suitable if: you are 18+ and comfortable with the basics of Ballet and want to progress your technique with new challenges and combinations. We'd recommend around one year of ballet experience for this class. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. sessions.title: Ballroom Beginners
sessions.details: Izzi blends the old elegance of Hollywood with the notion of deconstructing gender stereotypes. Expect empowering movements that celebrate strength and confidence for everyone, in a supportive and inclusive space. Learn a selection of dances over the term – from Foxtrot to Tango and Samba to Jive. Get ready for a joyful cardio workout without even realising you’re exercising. Izzi is a professional Ballroom and Latin dance instructor. She focusses on making Ballroom and Latin dance fit for the 21st century by deconstructing the gender stereotypes and homophobia traditionally embedded within couple dancing and making the ballroom world fairer for everyone. Suitable for: all if you are 18+, including complete beginners. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. Please make sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Please note, as the studios are used by our professional dancers we ask that you refrain from using hair products and body lotions as these can make the floor slippery. sessions.title: Contemporary Intermediate
sessions.details: In this class, Belinda will guide you through a series of exercises which blend the use of torso, fall and recovery, spatial pathways, flow and momentum. Drawing from her training in Cunningham, Limon and Release techniques, class will start with short technical exercises that build into more complex travelling steps, dynamic swings and longer choreographic phrases. In this class a sense of community and shared experience is created, providing an environment where participants feel safe, challenge themselves and above all, have fun. Suitable if: you are 18+ and you’ve taken a few months of contemporary dance classes before, are comfortable with the basics, and would like to develop your technique and creativity. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. sessions.title: Ballet Beginners
sessions.details: In this Beginners class, Nandita will share the basics and foundations of Ballet technique with a healthy and holistic approach encouraging supportive alignment, functionality and efficiency, focus, balance, coordination and strength. You will develop a deeper awareness of your body and relationship to the space, all while moving with musicality. As one of the few professional female ballet dancers of Indian heritage in the world, we’re so proud to welcome Nandita to our teaching faculty. After training at the Royal Ballet School, Nandita went on to perform with Zürcher Ballet, Victor Ullate Ballet, Ballet Black, Scottish Ballet and Compañia Nacional de Danza. Moving Together: Improvisation, Connection & Expression
sessions.details: In this class, James guides participants through improvisation practices that encourage honesty, curiosity, and personal expression through movement. Together, we will explore how to connect more deeply with ourselves, our bodies, and each other in a supportive and open environment. Through guided tasks and shared exploration, the class invites participants to discover joy in both dancing and witnessing others dance, while building a sense of community and connection. Rooted in playfulness and embodied practice, the sessions offer space to move freely, listen closely, and expand awareness through improvisation. Image by Yu-Ning Tan.

sessions.title: LIQUID FRAMEWORKS
sessions.details: The workshop will begin with a technique session, moving through various pathways, patterns, and sequences to activate, challenge, and open the body’s structure. The session will then move towards anatomical and imagery based improvisation, leading into partnering techniques and contact scores. Using the established vocabulary as a reference point, we will then deep dive into instant composition. With a focus on listening, adapting, and sensing, we will explore how communication and clarity in decision making and language can be tools to apply within group dynamics and theatrical images. This workshop will offer a space to analyse and further deepen the connection to your innate sense of expression, utilising technique and natural physical intelligence to slow down and open a bridge into creativity allowing freedom and ease within exploration.“

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Jemima Colins
sessions.details: Jemima's movement practice exists at the intersection of heightened listening, articulated expression and archival embodiment. The class is a combination of somatic mobilisations, improvisations and set materials; through which the accumulation of textures and embodiment can act as a tool to layer onto set material. Encouraging a communal collective exchange as well individual enquiry, through a class of high-physicality and awareness.

sessions.title: Gaga People
sessions.details: Gaga is the movement language developed by Ohad Naharin throughout many years, parallel to his work as a choreographer and artistic director (1990-2018) of Batsheva Dance Company. Gaga originated from Naharin’s need to communicate with his dancers and his curiosity in the ongoing research of movement. Gaga classes are predicated on a deep listening to the body and to physical sensations. The instructions are deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation, and rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Throughout the class, participants are guided by a series of evocative instructions deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation. Rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Participants should wear comfortable clothes and be prepared to dance barefoot or in socks. It is advisable to bring a bottle of water and a towel for use after class.

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: Couples Massage Workshop with RE-SET PAUSE
sessions.details: Massage is one of the most heartfelt ways to show care, a simple, meaningful way to connect through touch. Join us for a two-hour Couple’s Massage Workshop, designed for partners, friends, or family members who’d like to share a moment of relaxation and reconnection. You’ll learn gentle, soothing techniques, how to create a calming atmosphere, and ways to communicate through mindful touch for a deeply restorative experience. Fully clothed and performed on the floor, this practice is easy to recreate at home — with optional oils for extra comfort. The session is pregnancy-friendly and suitable for all levels. **Please note: this workshop is for personal enrichment and does not provide professional certification. One ticket per person is required.

sessions.title: THE LYMPHATIC PRACTICE
sessions.details: A two-hour, full-body self-massage workshop designed to introduce you to lymphatic drainage—or become part of your regular monthly body maintenance. Come with your partner, your mum, a group of friends or simply by yourself. Everyone is welcome. The lymphatic system is a body-wide network involved in fluid balance, immune function and transporting excess fluid and cellular debris away from the tissues. This workshop will help you understand why lymphatic work matters and teach you simple, practical techniques you can continue using at home to support comfort, recovery and ongoing health maintenance. The Lymphatic Practice is designed to be attended monthly, giving you the time and guidance to work slowly through the whole body while gradually learning the complete routine for yourself. Carli brings more than 20 years of hands-on experience and weaves together lymphatic self-massage, acupressure, Chinese medicine principles and clear Western physiology—explained in accessible, everyday language and made relevant to real life. **PLEASE BRING: Water and arrive well hydrated. A small body oil or cream that you already enjoy using. Comfortable clothing that allows easy access to the collarbones, chest and belly. Everything can also be practised over clothing if preferred.

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Alleyne Dance
sessions.details: This is a physical Contemporary Class, which will involve strong, complex and technical sequences in and out of the floor, focusing on quality, initiation, performance and stamina. Each session will begin with a different aspect of movement study, focusing on the articulation of hands, isolations, spirals, breath and flying. Improvisation will also be explored as part of self-development, stemming from a physical intention. The desired outcomes for the workshop are to develop the dancers' creative mind, driven from passion, determination, strength, musicality and most importantly an intention and honesty in whatever choice they make during the session.

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: LATIN-FUSION DANCE
sessions.details: A joyful, high-energy class blending Latin dance styles with contemporary movement and expressive flow. In this 60-minute session, you’ll explore rhythm, musicality, and full-body movement through accessible choreography and playful combinations. Open to all levels, the class offers options and variations so you can move at your own pace—whether you’re new to dance or looking to deepen your groove. Expect a supportive atmosphere, a good sweat, and plenty of space to connect with the music, your body, and the joy of movement. No partner needed. Come as you are, leave energised and inspired.

sessions.title: ProDance class with Hannah Thomas
sessions.details: This class will explore all things floorwork; from the gooey, melty improvisations to the highly exhilarating, ‘let the rhythm of the music take you for a ride’ phrase work. Hannah facilitates a friendly space for participants to explore with ease and encourages this through the use of music and individual feedback where possible. Expect a bubbly class, a spicy playlist and a lot of adrenaline.

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Camilla Curiel
sessions.details: Camilla's classes are energetic, expressive, and full of joy. Blending improvisation, instant composition, and dynamic movement phrases, each session invites participants to explore creativity through both body and imagination. Using imagery and emotion as a starting point, the classes encourage playful exploration, while collaborative composition tasks foster connection and collective creativity. Floorwork and release-based techniques are woven into movement sequences that challenge the body to generate energy, adaptability, and flow. The focus is on cultivating both physical vitality and creative curiosity in a supportive environment where playfulness, experimentation, and a willingness to explore are celebrated. Each class offers a slightly different experience while returning to a set of core principles, allowing participants to deepen their practice, discover new possibilities, and continue evolving from week to week.

In this 60-minute session, you’ll explore rhythm, musicality, and full-body movement through accessible choreography and playful combinations. Open to all levels, the class offers options and variations so you can move at your own pace—whether you’re new to dance or looking to deepen your groove. Expect a supportive atmosphere, a good sweat, and plenty of space to connect with the music, your body, and the joy of movement. No partner needed. Come as you are, leave energised and inspired.

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: Saturday CI x BMC® Workshop with Rick Nodine & Aki Omori: Moving from Within
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • This workshop introduces primitive reflexes, early developmental movement, and the organ system through the lens of Body-Mind Centering®. We will explore how these may support more fluid, responsive interactions in Contact Improvisation and expand our movement language with others, allowing expression to arise from within. We will start with a whole-body pattern to sense what an integrated, connected body feels like. From there, we will shift our attention to the soft core, investigating pathways for sequencing energy through the entire body, aligning inner experience with outward expression. This work is playful, intimate and engaging - fostering awareness, receptivity and enhanced responsiveness in Contact Improvisation. Photo by Lenka Rayn H https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-s6tun-20260523143000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1 (Course of 5 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-srouz-20260525183000

sessions.title: Saturday CI x Aikido Workshop with Rosalie Wahlfrid: The Power of Letting Go
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • In this workshop, we will explore the potential of the quiet body. Through movement and meditative practices, we will investigate how qualities such as softening, absorbing and deflecting may generate power, efficiency and responsiveness in movement. The workshop will introduce simple Aikido techniques alongside the fundamentals of posture and embodiment in Aikido and explore physical and mental states such as spatial awareness and internal focus. We will consider how these principles and techniques may support more fluid and responsive interactions in Contact Improvisation, while expanding our shared movement vocabulary. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sfc76-20260606143000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 11 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 01/06, 08/06, 15/06, 22/06, 29/06 and 06/07 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: It will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-smfda-20260629183000

sessions.title: Bound & Unbound Weekend, Autumn Edition: Exploring the Edges of Contact Improvisation
sessions.details: Anatomie Studio, Arch 113 Unit 17 Station Passage, London, SE15 2JR • A three day intensive with Jamus Wood & Rick Nodine. Contact Improvisation, Shibari & BMC®. In this short Intensive we will take time to explore some of the territory at the edges of Contact Improvisation. Exploring aspects of the dance that often go unrecognised or don’t receive quality attention. Contact improvisation, led by Rick, will be at the heart of our practice and the ground of our shared language. We will spend the first part of our time together dropping into inner and outer awareness through Body Mind Centering® exercises and perspectives. The intention is to bring a felt sense of embodiment and a deep listening to our dance. Later we will draw inspiration from Shibari (Japanese Rope Play) with Jamus. Initially, we’ll focus on the sensations of our bodies in relation to one another, without ropes yet through physical limitations, exploring binding and unbinding, being held and being free. We will then introduce ropes, engaging in Ichinawa (one rope technique) to explore further the qualities of resistance and surrender, stillness and breath, gravity and flow. A key aspect of our workshop will be The Switch —a playful exploration of roles as we transition between being bound and binding with one’s body. We will slow down and zoom in, lingering in each role for some time. Also taking moments when neither of us are in a role. We will emphasise consent throughout our time together. Consent will be taught as a practice so that we can dance within our limits while finding and exploring our edges together. We’ll conclude each day with an exploratory jam, allowing space to integrate what we've explored and to express ourselves freely, weaving our individual journeys into a collective tapestry of creativity and joy. Join us in this supportive circle of explorers. Together, let’s celebrate the borders of Contact Improvisation with Shibari, deepening our connections through movement, trust and shared discovery. Limited tickets available https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-stf0y-20261016183000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 12 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 07/09, 14/09, 21/09, 28/09, 05/10 and 12/10 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 02/11, 09/11, 16/11, 23/11, 30/11 and 07/12 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 6) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: This course will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sc3xz-20261102183000

sessions.title: 'ReSourcing your CI Practice: what moves you?' Workshop with Colleen Bartley
sessions.details: Room 154, Richard Hoggart Building, Goldsmiths, Lewisham Way, London, SE14 6NW • ReSourcing your CI Practice: what moves you? Working with foundational principles of CI this workshop explores Contact Improvisation as research into deep listening, tuning the senses and attention, emergent composition and self awareness. Over the course of the day we will explore quiet perceptual practices and more dynamic dancing, creating space for reflection, experimentation and embodied decision-making. Through touch, movement and attention, we will investigate how dances arise from changing relationships — between bodies, gravity, sensation, imagination and space. We'll explore how life moves through evolutionary patterns and work with materials from Nancy Stark Smith, Steve Paxton, Nita Little and other founders of CI with influences from Lisa Nelson, and Caryn McHose. The day will include solo, duet and group practices, scores, improvisational structures and time for reflection. We will explore responsiveness, composition in the moment, and ways of expanding perception through movement. We welcome curiosity, experimentation and different physical experiences. The class aims to cultivate an inclusive environment for curiosity, exploration, embodied research, critical reflection, dialogue and dancing together. Sources/Influences: Tuning Scores, Experiential Anatomy, The Underscore, Instant Composition, Neurological diversity, post-modern dance, Evolutionary Biology, BMC, Somatic Education, Relational Intelligence, Embryology, Functional Movement Colleen Bartley has a Dance and Education degree from Swarthmore College and a diploma in Community Dance from Laban with years of experience with Somatic Education. She co-organised London Contact Improvisation and was a co-editor at Contact Quarterly. She has worked directly with most of the founders of Contact Improvisation and been influenced by teachers of contemporary and post-modern dance, experiential anatomy with Gary Carter and Caryn McHose, Authentic Movement with Susan Schell, Improvisation & Composition (Tuning Scores with Lisa Nelson, The Underscore with Nancy Stark Smith, Ensemble Thinking with Nina Martin, Relational Intelligence with Nita Little) and is very active in dancing, organizing, writing about and documenting dance. Colleen has an invisible disability which informs her practice as a teacher and an artist. She believes that its everyone’s birthright to move, that people are inherently creative, movement is our first language, and sees dance as a way to empower people, to effect social change and to build community. sessions.title: THE ARC OF ATTENTION CI Class with Justin Philpott & Jam Soundscape by Carlo Natoli
sessions.details: Room 154, Richard Hoggart Building, Goldsmiths, Lewisham Way, London, SE14 6NW • A two hour Contact Improvisation class starting at 13:00 class followed by a jam at 15:00 finishing at 18:00. THE ARC OF ATTENTION This class explores circular movement as a pathway into contact improvisation. Beginning in stillness, we gently notice the journey of our awareness as we flow into self-led movement. From there, we explore circles, arcs and spirals through the body, allowing rolling, curving and looping pathways to emerge through improvisation. From this solo exploration, we gradually move into relation: first dancing with an awareness of others from a distance, then drawing closer, and eventually finding touch. We will then practise the skill of projecting from the ground, through the centre, and towards the point of contact with each other. With this experience in place, we return to circular movement and explore how contact becomes clearer: how we attend, meet, support and move with another through a shared point of connection. From there, the class opens naturally into the jam. About Justin: Justin is the host and resident teacher of the Brighton CI Community. He is a multidisciplinary mover with a background in martial arts and Thai-style bodywork. He has been dancing CI for over 12 years, teaching CI since 2018, and runs Moving Stillness - School of Somatics (https://www.moving-stillness.com). sessions.title: Contact Improvisation WORKSHOP w/ Ezra LeBank "Cloud Tectonics"
sessions.details: Laban Building - Car Park Studio, Creekside, London, SE8 3DZ • Cloud Tectonics: Training for Contact Improvisation & Contemporary Partnering “Is it possible for us to fly and fall without noticing much? Can the drift inherent in momentum compel us toward intuitive pathways above and along each other? We will begin with Dirt Work, physical training to expand, integrate, and ready our bodies in conversation with gravity and the earth. This prepares us for flight and dynamic capacity we explore in Cloud Tectonics, training that reframes our experiences of lift, loft, and drift. Detailed and buoyant exercises guide us toward a dancing experience full of abundant and radically free choice-making in vertical and spherical space for both ourselves and those we dance with. We imagine a dance we co-create amidst simultaneous independence and communion in flight. Ezra LeBank is a Professor of Movement and Chair of the Department of Theatre Arts at California State University Long Beach. Meditation, Aikido, and acrobatics work their way into his curiosity of CI. His approach is inspired by many wonderful teachers including Nancy Stark Smith, Ray Chung, Mike Vargas, Nita Little, and Steve Paxton. He has been invited as a teacher at International Contact Festival Freiburg, West Coast Contact Improv Jam, Seattle Festival for Dance Improvisation, Poland Contact Festival, Oberlin CI@50, and many more. Through his research company Bad Goat Dance, he studies Dirt Work & Cloud Tectonics as methods of bringing ourselves closer to the earth and to each other. www.badgoatdance.com https://bookwhen.com/cigoldsmiths/e/ev-sim4j-20261018110000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv: Class + Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This week we have a class taught by Marie, an experienced CI practitioner (22 years), professional dancer and choreographer. Theme and Content The theme of the class will be posted closer to the time in the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group. You can join in following this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (please note I will ask you a few question about yourself before I allow you into the chat, when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) These Contact Improvisation classes give participants tools to be in touch and communicate through touch, and feel more confident joining a jam. There are open levels and benefit beginners, improvers and experienced practitioners. There is a mix of somatic guided exploration to be embodied, usually in solo, some mindful and focused explorations with one or several partners, and some more technical tools or short patterns. This will be followed by a 45min-1h jam Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Event page: https://millco.co.uk/events/contact-improvisation-jam/ https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-scnfy-20260601183000

sessions.title: **Women’s Touch : Community as a relational process - workshop lab**
sessions.details: Siobhan Davies Studios, 85 Saint George's Road, London, SE1 6ER • Embodiment - Community - Develop self-enquiry and agency- Be in touch - Share reflection + Experiences + Food After the great success and feedback from the last Women's Touch event, I've decided to put together another one to follow-up on this inspiring and rich theme of Community as a relational process. What's different from the last one? More lab time, more time to co-create, journal and share impressions. We won't use yarns this time around but a different material... I'll reveal it later. What is it? Marie will facilitate this Contact Impro workshop/laboratory exploring how community forms through relation and difference. Weaving between movement scores and moments of shared reflection, participants are invited to experience connection in and out of contact. We will open up questions and investigations such as: -How do I enter and inhabit a group? -What helps me feel connected without erasing difference? -Is community something we belong to, or something we continuously make? Work unfolds through solo and group scores, supporting attentive connection, experimentation, and self-enquiry. The space intends to be safe, consent-based, and accessible to all. Rough schedule (may change slightly) 11.30am-12pm – Welcome tea & chat (meeting each other + time & space to land) 12pm –1.30pm – Intro to Consent, solo warm-up and collective embodied explorations 1.30-2.30pm – Lunchtime: food sharing 2.30-5.30pm – Group scores Small group reflection: community as a relational process Witnessing, writing, sharing and integrating Who is this for? Those who identify as women and non-binary interested in bringing more awareness to physical interactions in dancing and in Contact Improvisation It welcomes all levels and can be applied to other practices than Contact Improvisation. In the past people were able to apply it to dance therapy, theatre, psychology... This lab is open level. No prior experience of Contact Improv is required What is Women's Touch? Women’s touch is an event curated by Marie Chabert, that offers a space for those who identify as women and non-binary to explore movement practices that are mainly based on touch (Contact Improvisation, somatic practices, improvisation) in a safe environment. It aims to empower women to claim their space and redefine it within a framework that challenges prevailing patriarchal norms. It offers both a place to embody and share our experiences verbally. The intention is to foster a supportive environment, where participants feel safe to take risks, be vulnerable, and share their humanity, free from the pressure of dominant dynamics. Cultivating such spaces requires trust, shared language, and mutual care. It allows us not just to survive, but to thrive in connection. If you have financial difficulties and want to take part, please get in touch. photo by Sol Ji Park https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-sq6op-20260712113000

sessions.title: Contact Improvisation - Beginner's course (+revisiting fundamentals)
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 • Dates: Sept 24th to November 19th This course is for anyone curious about Contact Improvisation. It is open to both beginner dancers and those who have a bit more experience and want to revisit the fundamentals. Over 8 weeks you will learn to share weight and communicate through dance with the group or in partners. By the end of the course you should have the tools to join a Contact Improvisation jam and move confidently with other dancers. Each week, we will co-create a playful and safe space for experimentation and exploration. Every class will start with games and tasks to awaken our awareness of inner and outer space. Followed by integrating basic skills of Contact Improvisation in a simple and guided way. Practicing falling, rolling, floating, lifting and supporting, using gravity to move effortlessly. We will approach other themes such as touch and no touch, following and leading, support, structures and lifts (low table and high table), centre and extremities, shared weight and shared balance, upside down, head to tail connection, dynamics, and momentum. Please wear comfortable clothes. NB: the class on November 19th will take place at Chisenhale Dance Space (no wheelchair access) If you have any financial difficulties please get in touch with me directly mariechabert@orange.fr https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-su748-20260924183000

sessions.title: **Women’s Touch with special guest: Dr Vanio Papadelli**
sessions.details: Siobhan Davies Studios, 85 Saint George's Road, London, SE1 6ER • Embodiment - Community - Develop self-enquiry and agency- Be in touch - Share reflection + Experiences + Food Who is this for? Those who identify as women and non-binary interested in bringing more awareness to physical interactions in dancing and in Contact Improvisation It welcomes all levels and can be applied to other practices than Contact Improvisation. In the past people were able to apply it to dance therapy, theatre, psychology... This lab is open level. No prior experience of Contact Improv is required What is Women's Touch? Women’s touch is an event curated by Marie Chabert, that offers a space for those who identify as women and non-binary to explore movement practices that are mainly based on touch (Contact Improvisation, somatic practices, improvisation) in a safe environment. It aims to empower women to claim their space and redefine it within a framework that challenges prevailing patriarchal norms. It offers both a place to embody and share our experiences verbally. The intention is to foster a supportive environment, where women and non-binary participants feel safe to take risks, be vulnerable, and share their humanity, free from the pressure of dominant dynamics. Cultivating such spaces requires trust, shared language, and mutual care. It allows us not just to survive, but to thrive in connection. About Vanio Papadelli I am an interdisciplinary performance artist and educator based in London. I teach across HE Performing Arts Institutions (mainly Rose Bruford College and Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance) and as a freelancer. With movement and the senses at the core of my practice, I interact with other media including text, video, everyday objects and natural materials to create intimate, multi-layered, poetic and surreal environments as spaces of connection, reminiscence and change. My artistic practice explores raw and tender territories of vulnerability, memory, care and candidness in human relationships imbued in more-than-human worlds. I have dealt especially with mother-daughter relationships, female friendships, experiences of giving birth and mothering. My work is based in collaborative and interdisciplinary processes and has travelled in Greece, UK, Italy, Poland, Germany, Egypt and Lebanon. https://vaniopapadelli.com/ If you have financial difficulties and want to take part, please get in touch. photo by Sol Ji Park https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-s61bh-20261122110000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This weekly jam invites movers to jam together for a regular practice. Warming-up: Marie Chabert will facilitate the warming-up before the jam. The aim is for participants to arrive into their body, tune in, connect to themselves, to others and to the space around. It brings people into their senses and embodied awareness. It is not a class and doesn't give the same technical tools and principles as a class. Classes are held every other week and will give you these skills. Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners who took a few classes beforehand, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. sessions.title: Moving Encounters - An experiential workshop exploring embodied relational awareness for therapists and practitioners
sessions.details: Centre 151, 151 Whiston Road, London, E2 8GU • About the workshop A one-day experiential workshop exploring embodied awareness and relational presence through structured movement-based inquiry. This is a guided and contained space for working with attention, sensation, movement, and relation as they arise in real time. The emphasis is on direct experience rather than interpretation, performance, or technique. The day is structured, but not prescriptive, allowing space for both individual exploration and relational processes with others. The atmosphere of the day The workshop provides a structured experiential setting for exploring how awareness is organised in the body and in relation. At times the work will be internally focused and quiet. At other times it will involve movement in relation to others, with clear frameworks supporting consent, choice, and pacing throughout. Throughout the day, the intention is to stay close to what is actually happening in experience, moment by moment. Approaches informing the work This workshop draws on principles from: Body-Mind CenteringⓇ — somatic and developmental awareness of the body Authentic Movement — witnessed movement and reflective awareness Contact Improvisation — weight, responsiveness, and relational movement These are not taught as techniques, but used as reference points within structured experiential inquiry. What will be explored Across the day, the work will include: -attention to sensation, impulse, and movement -how awareness shifts between self and other -relational contact and distance -witnessing and being witnessed -patterns of responsiveness in interaction -how experience is received and registered in the body Participation is always invitational, and there is space to observe or pause at any time. Who this is for This workshop is open to therapists, counsellors, psychotherapists, and practitioners working in relational or embodied contexts. It is designed for those interested in exploring embodied awareness as part of their reflective practice, particularly those curious about how bodily experience shapes presence, attention, and relational responsiveness. No previous movement or dance experience is required. What this is not This is not: a dance or performance workshop a training in any therapeutic modality a group therapy or personal process group a space for psychological interpretation or treatment It is an experiential workshop for embodied inquiry and relational exploration. Reflection and integration There will be structured opportunities to reflect verbally on experience during the day. Reflection is offered as a way of noticing and articulating experience, rather than interpreting or analysing it. Participants are encouraged to consider how the work may relate to their own professional practice. About the facilitator This workshop is facilitated by Mark Rietema, a UKCP-registered Psychotherapist, trained in Process Work, and Somatic Movement Therapist (BMCA) with a background spanning clinical practice, somatic education, and movement facilitation. Alongside a clinical practice that has included extensive work within NHS mental health services, Mark teaches and facilitates in a range of professional and academic contexts, including Embody-Move UK, Institut Prozessarbeit Deutschland, and King's College London, where they contributed to research on arts and wellbeing in higher education. He teaches Body-Mind Centering within official BMCⓇ trainings in the UK, Spain, and Italy. Mark also teaches Contact Improvisation nationally and internationally, and is part of the organising team of the London Contact Festival and CI@Goldsmiths. This direct grounding in CI practice informs the relational and movement dimensions of the workshop. A background in community arts (MA, Goldsmiths) and experience facilitating internationally - including in the USA, Palestine, and Germany - continues to shape an approach that is both rigorous and attentive to the lived complexity of group work. Mark will be supported throughout the day by Sole de la Hoz, a Contact Improvisation teacher and trainee psychotherapist in Process Oriented Psychology, with a professional background in dance. Cancellation policy - full refund until 24th of May, 50% refund until 6th June, after that contact us to see if we can offer a transfer for a future workshop. https://bookwhen.com/markrietema/e/ev-s2y7g-20260621100000

sessions.title: Weaving Spatial Support into the Body, Laura Doehler
sessions.details: Rockingham Community Centre, Falmouth Rd, London SE1 6PD, UK • In this workshop we will explore how our weight always is supported by default and acts as support simply through being in space and sensing our own physical space. We strip back expectations around support to uncover how a changing physical landscape of body and space create a container that at times carries us through space and at other times means we become a carrier or both. Our intention is to challenge our ideas around support so we won't get locked into carrying or loading and acquire greater skills in falling through letting go and expansion. We will probe spatial anchoring by tapping into the expansive qualities that space offers, find lightness and the ability to redirect oneself. These processes shall support a greater freedom in our dancing inside and outside the studio as we reckon with our ideas and expectations around support.

sessions.title: London CI Weekender - 2-days of Contact Improvisation, Exploring the concepts of 'reaching and meeting' and 'elements of the jam' w/ Josh Jones and Lily Antonia
sessions.details:
Willesden, London, UK •

London CI Weekender
A 2-day Contact Improvisation Workshop

https://dandelion.events/e/londonciweekender

Whats on offer :

A weekend of movement, exploration, co-collaboration and connection. Diving into the fundamentals & philosophy of Contact Improvisation. The London CI weekender offers space and guidance to engage with the practice, tune into the body & develop the skills that serve us both in the dance and in daily life. Bringing shared inquiry to the foreground to drop deeper through the layers of what is possible through CI.

Each day has a distinct focus, and participants are welcome to attend either day or the full weekend.

Come deepen your connection to the ground, space, and others while gaining tools for (contact) improvisation, jamming, and attuned awareness through the joy of movement.

Saturday: Reaching & Meeting

How can we meet the earth, meet ourselves and meet another?

How is it to be met?

Investigating and understanding mutual meeting as a core part of the dance.

Reaching as a tool to transform into oscillating expansive movers. To expand awareness and expand the ability of the body. Coming away from collapse and into lightness. Effortlessly working with gravity and momentum.

The day will include technical insights and the approach is practice as research. Allowing ourselves to be informed by the dance - discover how to move functionally and fluidly, open to all that's available in the present. Through solo, partner & group exercises we’ll explore reaching and meeting as a shared point of attention.

This day offers a grounding in presence, deep listening, and mutual direction.

Sunday: Elements of the Jam


On Sunday, we move into the world of the jam. We’ll explore how to enter and exit dances, navigate shared space, and respond to each unfolding moment. Through structured improvisation scores and instant compositions, we’ll build tools for the jam, develop adaptability, and co-create through group improvisation.

A container for emergence and spontaneity.

Meet your facilitators

Lily Antonia (She/Her)

Dance & Movement Artist | Facilitator

Lily is a contemporary dance artist, specialising in contact improvisation. She has been performing, teaching and choreographing internationally since graduating from Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance. Working with companies Wired Aerial Theatre, Mad Dogs Dance Theatre, and Company Chameleon. Lily is co-director of contemporary dance and live art company UMAMI-i!-MOVEMENT and co-founder of Contact Improv MCR.

Her approach to CI blends playful exploration with technical clarity. Inviting curiosity, challenging potential and nurturing individual creativity - Lily invites dancers to bring an aliveness to the present. Creating spaces where dancers can listen, trust, and move with intention and spontaneity.

“To cultivate a state of being - in readiness without anticipation... we open ourselves to

all possibilities"

Joshua Jarvis Jones (He/They)

Dancer | Facilitator | Choreographer

Josh is a contemporary dancer and facilitator whose practice is rooted in emotional exploration and embodied connection. Following a time of personal loss, he found dance—especially contact improvisation—as a vital tool for healing, grounding, and rediscovering relationships with self and others.

Trained at the Northern School of Contemporary Dance, Josh has performed internationally with artists like Ricardo Buscarini and Madeline Shan, exploring themes of intimacy and identity. His deep engagement with contact improvisation bridges technique and relational psychology, and he shares this through workshops, labs, and festivals worldwide.

Josh co founded *Lean_In*, a nomadic movement series that has grown into the annual retreat *Lean_In_Nature*, inviting people into co-creative, embodied research. He has taught at CI hubs and circus events across Europe. His work invites participants into a dance of authenticity, where movement becomes a meeting place for truth and transformation.

INCLUSIVE AND SAFE SPACE

We are committed to creating an inclusive and safe space for all participants. This workshop is designed to be accessible to all and participants are welcome to let us know in advance about specific access needs.

Who’s the workshop for

Open to all levels. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or you've never done the practice before there is something for everyone. No previous dance experience required just a willingness to explore & create.

Where

Location will be given upon booking.

We will be dancing in the heart of Camberwell, the space has a kitchen available for use by participants, toilets and showers. Access to the hall is via a flight of stairs.

If you would like to attend but have financial concerns / are unable to purchase a ticket due to financial reasons please reach out - we will find the way with you.

This event is 18+

If you have any queries / questions / thoughts or just want to say hi please feel free to get in touch - leaninmovement123@gmail.com
